Life Framework: Everon 1989. Player manual

For the 0.3.0 alpha on the real Everon island. Written for players, not developers. Keep it on your phone or print it: manual.html is the same manual in one file, with every map inside.

The first ten minutes

  1. You wake in the hostel in Saint-Philippe. A waypoint and a mark on your map send you south to the town hall.
  2. Talk to the town clerk. You get your ID card, a welcome pack (bread, a sausage, a bottle of water and $100 in cash) and a starter car.
  3. Take the car out at the garage counter by the car lot, drive to the orchard, pick six apples and press them into juice at the stall.
  4. Sell the juice at the market stall in town. Each step shows its own waypoint, and the next errands wait under F2.
  5. Eat and drink from your inventory (Use). Press F on anything with a prompt: counters, signs, doors, ATMs.

What is live, and what is not (read this first)

This manual describes what is on the island today. Some systems exist in the code but have no placed site yet. Each is marked in the page that covers it.

LiveNot on the island yet
Parcel runs, the postal van run, taxi runs, wheat harvest with the reaper, lumber (by hand or by truck), fishing and the smokehouse, iron mining and smelting (Coalman's Brow, Highstone, the east smelter), coal (East Rise seam, the power plant buys it), scrap and the recycler, export orders at the dock, moonshine, chop shop, till robberies, the bank heist, the north rebel outpost, crews and the registry, police duty, medic duty, homes and plots for sale, cars and the truck yard, every shop in Saint-PhilippeGarbage round (only in the test grid). Fuel haul (no tanker depot on the island). Copper and stone (no copper seam, refinery or quarry is placed yet). Grain mill and bakery flour.

The other towns (Meaux, Montignac, Lamentin, Morton, Saint Pierre) are scenery for now. Everything you can do is in Saint-Philippe or at one of the work sites on the island map; the mines, the smelter, the truck yard and the north outpost are described in Jobs and Crime with their distances from town.

The alpha server in one paragraph

An in-game day is 2 real hours; nights pass twice as fast. The server restarts at 06:00 and 18:00 and warns you 15, 5 and 1 minutes before. You rejoin where you logged out (up to 12 hours). New characters get 5 minutes of grace: robberies and vault breaks refuse them. Homes and plots cost half their listed price, cars 80 percent, the firearm permit is instant, and the police desk approves applications at once. The alpha can be wiped; see the player FAQ.

1. Getting started

Waking up

A new character wakes on a bunk in the hostel (a town house just north of the main street; number 1 on the Saint-Philippe map). Step off the bed and go downstairs. The hostel and the square outside are safe zones: nobody can shoot you there.

You start with $2,000 in the bank and no cash, a work jacket, boots, and a folded paper map in your pack. After you die or rejoin you do not wake in the hostel again; see Money and Medic.

The welcome guide

A few seconds after you get out of bed a short welcome guide opens: five paper pages on what to do first (the town clerk, your starter car, then apples, juice and the market), money and the F2 "What to do next" page, the map, police and medic duty, and where to read more. Turn the pages with Next and Previous.

  • Set waypoint to the clerk (page 1) puts a waypoint on the town clerk, the first errand. If you are further along, it points at your current errand instead. Once every arrival errand is turned in, page 1 is headed WHAT NEXT and tells you to open F2 and pick What to do next, where Start on a row puts a waypoint on its first step.
  • Close puts it away; it opens again the next time you join, until the clerk has given you your papers.
  • Don't show again stops it opening by itself.
  • Press F3 (gamepad: right bumper + Y) to open it again at any time. You can change the key in Settings, Controls, Life Framework.
  • The handbook is under Handbook in the pause menu. It has ten short pages: your first wages, work in town, Trades and tools (levels, tool finishes, perks, the truck check), the police, Law and order (the charge sheet, fines, the cell), the hospital, if you turn to crime, The underworld (standing, the fence, the bars, the north outpost), Crews (the registry, flags, recruiting, the radio) and the law and the permit.

Your personal file

Press F2 (gamepad: hold right bumper + Y) to open your personal file. It has three tabs, and a fourth when you are in a gang:

  • Person: your name and role (civilian, police or medic, on or off duty), cash in hand and in the bank, houses owned, garage slots used, time on the island, whether you are wanted, the licenses and permits you hold, and your level in each job. Read on a job shows its title with your tier word (Apprentice, Hand, Journeyman, Foreman or Master), how far you are to the next level, what that level opens, the perks you picked and, once the shift boards are up, your rank in that trade this week. At level 10 and again at level 20 of a work trade, walk up to the labor office counter and take a perk for that trade: Double yield or Swift hands at 10; at 20 Light touch, the one you did not take, or Good word (traders pay you 10% more for that trade's goods; mining, logging, fishing and farming). Police officers pick at the dispatch board in the police station (Fast cuff or Long radar), medics at the dispatch board in the clinic (Quick revive or Quick aid at 10, Steady carry at 20). The first pick is free; changing it later costs $500 in cash at the same place, once a week per trade and level, and each trade has its own change row.
  • Progress: your first errands in order, each marked DONE, CURRENT or LATER, then any other errand you took. Read shows the errand and its progress; Set waypoint to the current errand puts it on your map.
  • Next: what you could do now to earn a living, with a line on each, roughly what it pays an hour and how far away it is. Only what you can already do is listed (police and medic duty show once you wear the badge), and nothing until the clerk has registered you. The run you are on is listed first and reads in progress; finished ones sink to the end and read Done. Pick one and press Start: a few short steps follow, each with a waypoint on your screen, a mark on your map and a one-line note. A step you have already done is skipped (you hold the job, you carry the tool). Resume on a started one puts the waypoint and the note back on its step. A row that pays nothing by the hour is marked no wage instead of a pay figure. Four more rows point you at a place on the island and show up when they apply: Found a crew (the registry cabin in Saint-Philippe; marked no wage; done once you are in a crew), Truck check (the examiner at the truck yard in the north-east, $300; listed at Hauling level 5 or when you own a van, done once you pass), Pick a perk (the counter at the labor office in the town hall; listed once any trade reaches level 10, done once you pick a perk) and A rumor of easy money (the fence's yard; listed once you have a criminal record). Start puts the waypoint on the place.
  • Gang (only if you are in a gang): your crew at a glance, read only. The gang's name and flag, your rank, which members are online, whether a radio you carry is on the gang channel, and the sites the gang holds. It shows only your own gang. Nothing on it is a standing number; gang standing is never shown as a figure.

Your current objective

The step you are on stays written under your money at the top right ("Next: Mine 15 iron nuggets"). It flashes gold when it changes and stays until the step is done, even after the note fades. After a rejoin the waypoint, the line and the step's note come back by themselves. Type /hud objective off in chat to hide the line.

Your welcome pack and car

The clerk gives you your ID card, some cash and a meal; a note lists everything you got. A small car waits in the garage at the car lot next to the town hall. When you take it out, one note gives its plate (it replaces the "waiting on the pad" note instead of standing beside it), its hazard lights blink and a marker sits over it for 30 seconds, so you can tell it from the other cars on the lot.

The mining run, step by step

StepWhat you do
Take the miner jobThe desk by the mine on Coalman's Brow, south-west of the square
Buy a pickaxeThe miner's supply counter beside the mine desk ($150); the hardware store and general store sell one too. Skipped if you carry one
Take your car outYour garage; any car will do (the buyer is down at the dock). Skipped if a car is already out or you own none
Go to the mineBack up to Coalman's Brow
Mine 15 iron nuggetsSwing at the rust-veined rocks and pick up the pieces, one full furnace load. Every piece levels Mining; level 4 opens the East Rise coal seam
Smelt your barsThe mine furnace: 3 nuggets make a bar, so 15 make 5 bars in one 4-minute run
Sell your barsThe iron counter in the dock wholesale warehouse, $20 a bar. The mine adds $180 for your first run, so you finish about $130 ahead after the pickaxe

The other starters are shorter: the postal van run (a driving license, the post stand at the parcel kiosk, one run to Meaux and back), lumber (the lumberjack job, an axe, a felled tree), fishing (a rod, the nearest water, a fish), the apple harvest (the orchard, 5 apples, a bottle of juice; the arrival route below uses six apples and makes two), and police or medic duty (the duty desk, clock in).

The file only shows what the records office holds; nothing in it can be changed from there. Esc or Close puts it away.

The arrival quest

A quest panel on screen tells you what to do next. Each step puts a waypoint with a distance on your screen and a mark on the open map. The marks move on by themselves when you finish a step. If you log out half way, the mark comes back when you rejoin. Other players do not see yours.

StepWhat you doWhere
New in townWalk south from the hostel to the town hall. Talk to the town clerk ("Town clerk: ID cards"). He writes your name in the register and hands you your ID card and a welcome pack: bread, a sausage, a bottle of water and $100 in cash.Town hall on the square
Your first carThe clerk also puts a small Sputnik T601 in your garage. It is yours, and it takes one of your garage slots. Walk to the garage counter at the car lot and pick Retrieve vehicle; the car stands on the garage pad and your key is already in your pocket.Car lot, west of the town hall
Apple pickingDrive to the orchard east of town and pick six apples from the apple trees.Orchard
Fresh juiceUse the juice press on the orchard stall: three apples make one bottle of apple juice, so your six make two.Orchard stall
Sell your juice at the market stallSell your apple juice to the market trader in town: look at the stall, scroll down to the juice row (the last one, Sell 1 Apple Juice; the row shows the price, $18 a bottle) and press F, or pick Sell all goods. The sale note reads Sold for $18!, then a card titled Find steady work reads You are on your way: take a job from the town board, ask the clerk for more errands, and find your errands and jobs in your player menu.Market

You get the welcome pack and the car once per character, never again after a respawn, a rejoin or a server restart. A character who already owns a car gets no starter car: take your own car out of the garage for that step. A character who registered before this route existed is guided through the steps they have not done yet.

After the market sale the clerk has seven more errands. They show under F2, Progress, in this order: Five parcel runs (five paid runs at the post office open fuel delivery), Your first fuel run, Your own wheels (get the driving license at the town hall, then buy a car at the car lot), A firearm permit (the gun store counter), Sell a catch (land a fish and sell it at the dock), A plot of your own (read the sign on a plot for sale) and Lay your foundation (gravel and cement come from the hardware store).

Your bank account also starts with money in it: use an ATM to take some out or put your cash away. Cash in your pocket is lost if you die; money in the bank is not.

The town hall also sells licenses

The same clerk's desk issues the driving license ($100, taken from your bank account first, then from your pockets). You need it to buy a car. The firearm permit ($250) is bought at the gun store counter, and in the alpha it is instant. A truck license ($300) comes from the examiner at the truck yard in the north-east: you drive a lent truck through four gates in order. Miss a gate and the fee is lost, with a short wait before you can try again.

The map and waypoints

  • Open the map: press M. If nothing opens, take the folded paper map out of your pack and hold it; every new character carries one. The map opens centered on you at town zoom, and closing it puts the paper map back in your pack.
  • Every kind of place has its own icon, a round badge coloured by group (green shops, orange food, blue travel, brown work, dark blue police, red health). No two kinds share an icon. Point at an icon to read its name.
  • The key on the right edge of the map lists every icon on your map, grouped, with its name. Point at a row and those places grow and pulse on the map while the rest fade. Click a row to show only that kind (click again for all); click a group's heading to open or shut its rows (every group starts shut). The Key tab under your cash folds it away, and the map remembers that.
  • Icons that share one spot show the most important one and a count; click it to zoom in. Zoomed far out, a slate badge with three dots stands for a group of places. Places you have not seen yet may show as "heard of" until you walk past.
  • Set your own waypoint: Shift + Left click on the map (gamepad: hold Y, press A), or just click a place. It shows on the map as a bold red ring with its name and distance, and in the world as a marker with the distance. There is one waypoint at a time; a new click moves it. The same click on the waypoint, or Backspace (gamepad: double-tap Y), clears it.
  • How to use the map: the card in the bottom-left corner lists these controls for your mouse or gamepad, and the waypoint set now. F1 (gamepad: click the left stick) folds it to one line; the map remembers that too.
  • Safe zones are a soft green tint with a small label under their edge. Find a place on the left searches by name.
  • The notice board and the Taxi and courier jobs set waypoints for you.
  • Scale: Saint-Philippe is about 450 m across. The whole island is about 12 km. See the maps.

What the screen shows

The screen stays almost empty. A few small figures sit at the edges and fade when nothing changes:

  • Top right: money. The cash you carry in large figures, your bank balance under it. When cash changes the difference slides in beside it (+$100 in green, -$18 in red) and fades. After a few seconds the block dims; it comes back to full brightness on any change and while the inventory or the map is open.
  • Under the money: wanted badges. Up to five small badges fill with your wanted level. They flash red and read Wanted for a moment when the level goes up, and disappear when you are clear.
  • Bottom center: food and drink. Hidden while both are above half. They appear when one drops below half, for a few seconds after you eat or drink, and the number turns red below 25.
  • Bottom right: health and stamina, shown while they change.
  • Top left: a small Life Framework mark.

The HUD hides behind full-screen menus and during a conversation. Type /hud in chat to switch a part off or on: /hud money off, /hud wanted on, /hud needs off, /hud brand off, or /hud all on. The choice is kept on your PC.

Eating and drinking

You get hungry and thirsty over real time: from full, hunger runs out in about 2 hours 45 minutes and thirst in about 2 hours 15 minutes. Below 20 your health starts to drop slowly. Needs never kill you outright, but you will be weak and the screen tells you.

  • Open your inventory, pick a food or drink and press Use. You raise the item to your mouth and about 5 seconds later the gauge goes up (a loaf of bread is about +25 hunger). The item is used up.
  • Or put the food in a quick slot, hold it and press the use input. A stack loses one unit per use.
  • You cannot eat or drink while cuffed, downed, driving or swimming. A toast says so and nothing is used.
  • Hold a tin and press G to throw it. It flies ahead and lands; pick it up again.

Where to buy food: the supermarket, the general store, the bakery, the butcher, the cafe, the newsagent and the fuel kiosk at the filling station. Prices are in the shop list.

Staying safe in the first minutes

  • Grace: for your first 5 minutes of play, robberies and vault breaks refuse you with a message. After that you are fair game.
  • Safe zones: the square (52 m round the town hall) and the hostel (25 m). The bank and the gun store are just outside.
  • Restarts: at 06:00 and 18:00 server time. A toast warns you at 15, 5 and 1 minutes. Finish what you are doing and stand somewhere safe.

2. Money

Cash and bank

  • Cash is what you carry. Shops, the fuel pumps and homes take cash. Cash in your pocket is lost if you die (it stays on your body for someone to search).
  • Bank money is safe. Your balance starts at $2,000: enough for the cheapest car, the driving license, a pickaxe, an axe and an entrenching tool, plus three $150 respawn bills if you die, with a little over for fuel and food. Every car costs more than $500, so cars are paid from the bank; deposit first.
  • A small benefit of $50 is paid every 20 minutes while your money is almost gone (under $250), so nobody is ever stuck.
  • Job pay arrives as cash. Police and medic pay is handed out in cash when you clock out. Carry less, bank more.

ATMs and the teller

Three ATMs stand in Saint-Philippe. Walk up to one and look at the part you want; no window opens.

  • Take cash out: look at the wide CASH slot. Scroll the mouse wheel to pick Withdraw $20, $50, $100, $500 or Withdraw all, then press F.
  • Put cash in: look at the DEPOSIT drawer below it. Pick Deposit all cash, $50, $100 or $500, then press F.
  • See your balance: the machine's green screen shows your bank balance and the cash you carry while you stand at it, and it updates after every transaction. Only you see your figures. Check balance on the screen also shows them in a short message.

A line you cannot afford is grayed out and says why (Not enough in the bank, Not enough cash on you). On a gamepad, cycle the lines the same way as on any other object with several actions. To send money to another player's account, look at the keypad and pick Bank transfer. You can also talk to the teller at the bank counter; it does the same thing.

The three ATMs are on the bank wall, on the east side near the filling station, and on the dock; they are marked ATM on the Saint-Philippe map.

Transfers: Bank transfer on the keypad opens the transfer page. It shows your own account number; key in the recipient's number and the amount and press SEND. There is no fee, and one account can send up to $50,000 a day. To hand over cash instead, look at the player, press F to open the player menu and pick Give cash.

What you earn

About $400 an hour from courier work, $400 to $500 from harvest, lumber, fishing or apple juice once you have the kit, $480 to $560 an hour on medic duty and $350 to $450 on police duty (the duty bonus adds a little, up to $600 and $520 an hour). Duty is steady pay, not the best pay: a skilled trade with a van or a truck earns more than an officer. The jobs are in Jobs.

Levels. Every paid run, felled tree, fish and revive earns job experience. Higher levels unlock the next job (fuel delivery at Delivery level 4, about 3 paid parcel runs on this server; taxi at level 6, about 6) and licenses (felling, sawing, tools). A refusal message says what is missing and where to get it.

What each level opens. The level-up card and the F2 skill card name what a level really gives you. A level that opens nothing says so: it reads "Mining 13: steady and sure" and promises no perk. The levels that open something (a license, a machine step, a perk pick, a fish, a delivery job) are these; every other level from 2 to 30 is a milestone.

First shift of the day. The first 30 minutes you earn experience in a trade each day pay double. The clock starts at your first paid outcome, not when you clock in. After the 30 minutes the rest of that day pays the normal rate. Each trade has its own first shift, and a new day opens it again. A server restart opens it again too.

Working beside a learner. If you are level 10 or more in a trade and earn experience within 15 meters of someone under level 10 in the same trade, you both get a small bonus (a tenth of the award). It works the other way round too, when the learner earns. A pair can earn it once a minute, and your own other characters do not count.

Night pay. Parcel, postal van, fuel and taxi runs finished between 21:00 and 05:00 game time pay 25 percent more. A game day is 2 real hours and the night passes twice as fast, so the window lasts about 20 real minutes in every 2 hours.

Runs on the map. Hover a job's badge on the map (M) and the whole run is drawn: dashed lines join its stops in order with numbers 1, 2, 3... and the card says where you are, e.g. Mining run: step 2 of 5, next: ore rocks. Runs: mining, apples, postal van, lumber and fishing. A stop you have not found yet stays off the map.

Parcel runs (courier)

Status: ✅ live.

  • Where: the post office counter (map name Parcel depot) on the main street, west of the hostel. The drops are mailboxes on house walls in the east districts and along the dock.
  • How to start: press F at the counter, pick Take courier work (once), then Pick up parcel. The pickup asks for a small refundable cash deposit for the cargo. The note that follows names the amount and says it comes back on delivery.
  • What you do: carry the parcel to a mailbox at least 300 m from the counter. The pickup note sends you to "the delivery stop marked on your map" and a waypoint marks it. At the box pick Complete the run. You cannot deliver instantly: a drop that is too close, or reached too fast, pays nothing and keeps your run. Abandon the run at the counter if you give up; you get no pay and lose the deposit.
  • Pay: $40 a run ($50 at night). About 6 minutes a run is $400 an hour. A harbor contract run pays more once you have standing with the harbor master.
  • Needs: nothing, and no license. Every paid run counts toward the next job.

The drops are on the east side (a house near the district road) and four along the dock; the post office is on the Saint-Philippe map.

Postal van run

Status: ✅ live. A beginner job: no work level needed.

  • Where: the post stand on the side wall of the post office kiosk in Saint-Philippe (map badge Post office (van run)). The far office is the stand beside the newspaper kiosk on the Meaux square, about 1.3 km south down the coast road.
  • How to start: press F at the stand and pick Take the postal van run. A yellow post van is parked beside the office, locked, and its key is in your pocket: only you can drive it. One van at a time.
  • What you do: pick Load or unload a mail sack four times at the home stand with the van beside it. Drive to Meaux (the waypoint shows the way), park by the stand there and unload the four sacks the same way. Drive back, park by the home stand and pick Hand in the postal run.
  • Pay: $80 a run ($100 at night), plus delivery work experience. About 10 minutes a run is $480 an hour. A run handed in faster than 7 minutes pays nothing: the start toast and the hand-in say so, and the run stays open so you can hand it in later.
  • Lose the run: wreck the van, or leave it and stay more than 350 m away for 3 minutes, and the run ends with no pay (after 2 minutes away a toast warns you how many seconds are left); the van goes back to the office. Give up the postal run at a stand does the same at once. A new van is ready a minute later.
  • Needs: a driving license ($100 at the license desk). The van is lent, never yours: it is not saved and cannot be garaged.

Fuel delivery

Status: ✅ live. Needs Delivery level 4 (about 3 paid parcel runs).

  • Where: sign up at the post office counter. You take a fuel can at the filling station and carry it to a fuel drop, a drum in a farm yard on the edge of the village or under the sheds above the quay.
  • What you do: pick the fuel work at the post office counter, take the can at the station, carry it to a drop and use the drop-off action. A drop that is too close to where you started is refused: take it to a farther one.
  • Pay: $75 a run ($94 at night). About 8 minutes a run is about $560 an hour, and every run counts toward your Delivery level.
  • Needs: Delivery level 4. No license.

Taxi

Status: ✅ live. Needs work level 6 (about 6 paid parcel runs) and another player in your car.

  • Where: the taxi rank at the clinic corner. A beige cab waits at the curb. Sign up at the post office counter (Take taxi work), then press F at the rank for Start fare.
  • What you do: pick the passenger up, drive to the stop on your waypoint, and complete the run with the passenger still seated.
  • Pay: between $90 and $150 a fare by distance; a 2 km trip pays about $100. About $600 an hour with a steady stream of fares.
  • Needs: work level 6 and a real passenger seated in the cab when you drop them off.

Getting around by bus

Status: ✅ live. Not a job: the cheap way to reach work before you own a car.

  • Where: the bus stop signs (a round blue bus plate on a yellow pole) at the curb, shown on the map as Bus stop. Every stop has a printed timetable board on its pole: the line's name, this stop marked You are here, then every other stop, nearest first, with its fare. Walk up to it and read it.
  • How: look at the sign and scroll the action list: one line per stop, nearest first, such as Bus to Harbor: $18, 20 s. Press F on the one you want: the fare comes out of your cash (not the bank). There is no window. A grayed line tells you why: Not enough cash, Police nearby (when you are wanted), Next bus not due yet or Ticket already bought.
  • The wait: 20 to 30 seconds at the stop; a hint counts it down. The screen fades, and you stand beside the sign at the stop you picked. Changed your mind? Cancel trip (refund) is on the same sign while you wait.
  • Fare: $15 plus about $6 a kilometre, never more than $45.
  • Cancelled and refunded: walk more than a few meters from the sign, get hurt or start a fight, go down, get cuffed or climb into a vehicle while you wait. You get the fare back.
  • Refused: no ticket while dead, downed, cuffed or jailed, in a vehicle, in a fight, or wanted with the police close by. After a ride, the next bus is a minute away.

Harvest and farm

Status: ✅ wheat harvest, vegetable plots, beehives and orchard are live. There is no mill or bakery flour yet.

  • Where: the wheat field at the south-west edge of town: a contract board at the gate and a weighbridge south of it. The farm supply counter and the implement rack are in town beside the farm.
  • How to start (wheat): buy the reaper at the farm supply counter ($1,200, you keep it for good), or take a rental kit from the contract board (a $300 deposit that comes back when you return it; it comes with a vehicle). At the rack, use Take out reaper to hitch it behind a UAZ469 or Z7211.
  • What you do: at the board pick Post contract (once per ripe field), then Take with own reaper or Take with rental kit. Drive slowly over the wheat (the reaper cuts a 3 m bar between 2 and 20 km/h; faster or slower cuts nothing). The hopper fills at 10 kg a 3 m square and holds 600 kg. Drive to the weighbridge, stay on the scale and pick Sell grain (the market price, falling a little per lot and recovering through the hour) or Bag grain. Return kit at the board when you are done.
  • Pay: about $416 an hour selling grain, rising a little with a good price. The field grows back, so you can go round again.
  • Needs: the reaper and a vehicle to tow it. Buying a car needs the driving license.
  • Smaller jobs: a vegetable plot at the farm (plant cabbage seeds, water, harvest; sell cabbage at the market stall for about $4), the beehives (honey sells at the market stall from about $8 falling to $4; a hive kit is $120), and the orchard (take the farmer job at the desk and gather apples and plums; wholesale pays about $5 and $4 and falls as you sell). These are pocket money next to the wheat.

Lumber

Status: ✅ live. The timber yard at the village edge and the island sawmill both work.

  • Where: the timber yard (sign Sawmill) on the western edge of town, with a lumberjack desk and a saw. The timber counter (We buy timber) is on the curb of the hardware store on the south-east road. The island sawmill is far to the south (about 5.6 km); see the island map.
  • How to start: take the lumberjack job at the desk. Buy an axe ($120) at the hardware store.
  • What you do:

With a van or truck, back it up to the saw (rear within about 3 m): when you carry no logs, the action reads Feed from the truck and the saw takes the logs straight from the vehicle and puts the cut back in it. A locked vehicle feeds nothing. Every processing station works this way. 3. Sell planks ($8) and hardwood boards ($15) at the timber counter. If its purse is full it tells you to "try the wholesale warehouse at the dock". The dock pays a lower, falling price for planks, boards, posts and firewood.

  • Pay: about $400 an hour carrying softwood by hand. With a truck and hardwood boards, about $700 to $800 an hour: the timber counter takes about 28 boards an hour at $15, and the rest sell at the wholesale counter beside it for less.
  • Needs: an axe. Job levels unlock sawing and faster felling (a refusal says what is missing).
  • Shift board: at the island sawmill a cork shift board stands under the roof at the front of the hall, a few steps from the lumberjack desk. Read the shift board lists the week's top five workers at the sawmill by the trade XP they earned there, with their trade level. The list empties every Monday at 06:00 UTC.

60SawmillLumberjack desk and two saws inside the hall.

Fishing

Status: ✅ live. You can catch, smoke and sell fish: the wholesale warehouse on the dock buys every fish and every smoked fish at a fixed price.

  • Where: three spots. Spring Pond has a jetty in town, south-east of the square. Fisherman's Bay is a sheltered cove on the west coast (Gaspard, the old man on the bench in town, tells you about it once you land three fish). Black Lake is far to the south-east. The smokehouse is on the dock.
  • How to start: buy a fishing rod ($60) and a bait tin ($30) at the seed and feed store.
  • What you do: hold the rod, aim at the water within casting range and fire to cast. Wait 15 to 60 seconds for a bite: the float is pulled under. Fire again within 2 seconds to land it. You can cast about 6 times a minute. Bait makes bites faster. A spot holds about 14 fish and refills one fish every 90 seconds. The pond gives perch, carp and trout; the bay and open sea give mackerel, bass and tuna; the fish depend on the time of day.
  • Smokehouse: put a fresh medium fish and one firewood bundle in the smoker; 30 seconds later you have a smoked fish.
  • Selling: walk into the wholesale warehouse on the dock (the same counter that buys planks, iron bars and cement), press F on the clerk's counter and sell the fish. It pays a fixed price, the same every time (no falling price), and takes a whole stack in one go:

| Fish | Small | Medium | Large | Smoked | |---|---|---|---|---| | Trout | $4 | $12 | $22 | $18 | | Perch | $3 | $11 | $19 | $16 | | Mackerel | $3 | $7 | $13 | $16 | | Carp | $5 | $13 | $24 | $21 | | Bass | $5 | $10 | $21 | $23 | | Tuna | $10 | $20 | $39 | $43 |

  • Pay: a spot refills one fish every 90 seconds, about 40 fish an hour once its first stock is fished out; between those, the same water keeps giving small fish (a little slower). That is about $430 an hour at Spring Pond or Black Lake and about $470 at the cove at Fisherman's Bay, and more in the first hour while the stock lasts. Bass bite only in the evening (17:00 to 21:00); the rest of the day the cove gives mackerel. Smoking a medium fish (plus a firewood bundle) turns $7 to $13 into $16 to $23, so the smokehouse is worth the walk when you have fish to spare.
  • Needs: rod and bait.

Scrap and recycling

Status: ✅ live. The yard works and the garage mechanic in Saint-Philippe buys scrap metal, copper wire and rubber scrap. Iron bars sell at the dock wholesale yard.

  • Where: the scrapyard (sign Scrapyard) east of town, about 450 m east-north-east of the filling station.
  • How to start: walk in. No sign-up.
  • What you do: search the scrap piles for scrap metal, rubber, copper wire coils, worn hand tools and old radios. At the recycler bench pick Load with an item, hold Work (each worker adds one unit, so two people finish twice as fast) and Collect the parts. A worn tool gives scrap metal, an old radio gives metal and wire, car parts give 3 iron bars.
  • Selling scrap: take it to the garage (map name Garage, the mechanic's counter in the districts; see the Saint-Philippe map), press F at the till and sell. The mechanic pays half the catalog price, a fixed price with no stock limit and no questions about where it came from: scrap metal $4, copper wire coil $12, rubber scrap $5. He does not buy stolen goods or the worn tools and old radios (break those down at the bench first).
  • Pay: a bench load (a worn tool is $12 of metal, an old radio is $20 of metal and wire) and the loose finds come to about $100 to $200 an hour at one search every four minutes, a side income and not a main job. Iron bars sell for about $20 each at the dock wholesale yard and fall as you sell. Car parts cost $200 at the garage, so buying them to recycle loses money; the yard is for parts you find or chop.
  • Needs: nothing.

#PlaceWhat
60ScrapyardSearch the scrap piles; the recycler bench is in the yard.
61Recycler benchBreak car parts and scrap into metal.

Garbage round

Status: ❌ not on the island yet. The route job is built and tested in the test grid only. No depot desk, truck or dump is placed.

The plan: take the garbage round at a depot desk, drive the company truck to the 5 nearest bins in order, Empty bin at each, and Tip the load at the dump. The truck opens only for you. It pays $15 a bin plus a $25 bonus, $100 a round (about $400 an hour, no buy-in).

Fuel haul

Status: ❌ not on the island yet. The code and a fuel depot yard at Montignac exist, but no fuel pickup or depot desk is placed, so the run cannot start.

The plan: buy a 1,000-litre load at the Montignac depot at $0.90 a liter (the locked depot tanker then opens for you alone), pump it into a station tank and earn $1.35 a liter (a $450 margin per haul, about $450 an hour). The filling station pumps in town sell from a 3,000-litre tank ($2 a liter). If the tank runs dry the pump says "The tanks are dry. The depot truck is due."

Mining

Status: ✅ live. Iron is mined at Coalman's Brow, the hill just south of the village, and at Highstone; coal is cut at the East Rise seam. Copper, gold and stone are not on the island yet.

  • Where: the iron mine (sign Coalman's Brow mine, map label Iron mine) on the wooded north side of the brow, about 350 m south of the square past the farms; the track off the road to the west leads up to it. It has the miner's desk, a miner's supply counter, six rust-veined iron rocks at the foot of a granite rock face, and a furnace. The pickaxe is sold at the supply counter beside the desk, at the hardware store on the south-east road and in the general store.
  • How to start: take the miner job at the desk by the mine (Take the job: Miner on its clock). A desk job such as miner, lumberjack or farmer now stays with you after a restart and after a respawn. Then buy a pickaxe ($150) at the supply counter. Any new miner can buy it.
  • What you do:

A rock gives 5 pieces, shrinks as you work it, then crumbles and grows back after about 5 minutes. Each piece is miner XP. 2. Take the nuggets to the furnace and choose Smelt iron nuggets: 3 nuggets make 1 iron bar. One run smelts up to 5 bars in 4 minutes; keep mining while it works, the bars drop at the furnace when it is done. Every finished batch is Smelting XP, a trade of its own with its own level; it is not Miner XP. 3. Sell the bars at the iron counter in the wholesale warehouse at the dock, east of the main counter ($20 a bar; it buys 40, then about 24 more an hour). If it says it is full, the main wholesale counter buys more (from $20 a bar, falling as you sell).

  • Pay: about $450 an hour at the brow, with nothing to drive. Two players share the six rocks and the furnace comfortably.
  • The second rung (Smelting and Mining levels):
  • Shift board: a cork shift board stands in the mine yard near the miner's desk. Read the shift board lists the week's top five workers at the mine by the trade XP they earned there, with their trade level. The list empties every Monday at 06:00 UTC.
  • Wear: every swing at a rock wears the pickaxe you swing a little (an axe wears with each tree felled, a fishing rod with each fish landed). Each tool keeps its own condition: a new pickaxe starts in top shape whatever your old one looked like, and a worn one stays worn in your pack, on the ground, in someone else's hands and after a restart. A notice names the tool when it is getting worn, when it is badly worn, and after every use once it is worn out. A worn-out tool still works. At the hardware bench, hold the tool you want fixed: $12 and a scrap of metal bring that one tool back to top shape.
  • Better tools: the miners' supply till in the hardware store also sells the pickaxe, axe and fishing rod in three finishes: worn ($150), standard ($600) and fine ($1,800). A better finish wears slower: a worn tool loses twice as much per use as a standard one, a fine one half as much. The standard pickaxe or axe needs trade level 3 and the fine one level 6; below that the till refuses in words.
  • Needs: the miner job and a pickaxe. Mining 4 opens the coal seam and Mining 12 the rich Highstone rocks; the level-up card at Mining 2 names the coal permit and says so (the seam still needs Mining 4). The island has no copper or gold rock, so no card names a copper or gold permit. The smelter, the refinery and the cement works are Smelting work: batches there earn Smelting experience, and the iron smelter takes anyone from Smelting level 1 (you earn the trade by smelting), while the copper refinery (Smelting level 15) and the cement works (level 6) are not on the island yet. At the iron smelter the level grows the run: up to 6 bars at level 2, 7 at level 5, 8 at level 8 and 10 at level 16, and the run itself drops from 60 to 45 seconds at level 7 and to 35 at level 9 (the level-up card names each one). Where a trade has a level gate, the refusal says it in words: "Needs Smelting 15".

Export orders

Status: ✅ live. The board stands on the warehouse wall at the dock and the crane spot is on the quay.

  • Where: the EXPORT ORDERS board on the warehouse wall by the quay, and the crane spot (a pallet box on the quay apron by the harbor crane).
  • How it works: the board lists up to three orders, such as 40 x iron bars to the steamer | $1040 by 23:00; a new order opens every 30 game minutes while a slot is free. Scroll to Take the order on a line to take it (haulers at Delivery level 10 or higher; one order at a time). Bring every unit to the crane spot, in your pockets or in a vehicle backed up to the pallet box (a truck holds every order's full count), and choose Hand in the export order.
  • Pay: the order's price in cash (the market's wholesale price plus 15 percent, plus an order bonus) and Delivery experience. Every kind of order pays about $700 an hour of mining or sawing: 40 iron bars $1,040, 100 coal $985, 120 planks $1,018. A short count takes nothing: bring the rest and hand in again. Miss the deadline (20 game hours for iron, 24 for coal, 30 for planks) and the order closes and your standing in town drops; it never costs money.
  • Copper: the board offers no copper order, because no copper seam is placed on the island yet. It comes back with the copper chain.
  • Paper: a paid shift hands you a payslip, a parcel run a delivery note, and a sale at the granary or a buyer a weigh slip. Each shows what was sold or paid and the date; choose Read receipt on it to read it.

4. Homes

Saint-Philippe has 32 homes for sale and 4 building plots. Every other building is a shop, a civic building, a resident's own house (locked, with a brass name plate) or a barn and lock-up (locked).

Buying a home

  1. Walk to a house with a For sale sign on its wall. The sign shows the tier ("Cottage", "Village house", "Family house", "Town house", "Farmhouse" or "Villa") and the price.
  2. Carry the price in cash. Withdraw it at an ATM first; homes are not paid from the bank.
  3. Stand within 5 m of the sign and press F. Pick Buy house. The money leaves your hands and the sign shows sold.
  4. A house key goes into your inventory. The key is bound to that house.

There is no sell-back.

Keys and locks

  • Every home door is locked for everyone but its owner and key holders. An owner (or key holder) presses F at the door to lock or unlock it.
  • Your key opens your door. A stranger needs a key or a lockpick (see Crime).
  • Your home stays yours after a server restart.

Spawning at home

Stand at your door and pick Make this my spawn. One home at a time: choosing a second one clears the first. If you sell or lose the house the spawn goes back to the default. A rejoin still puts you where you logged out (within 12 hours).

Plots

A plot is an empty building site with a For sale sign. Buying one is the same as a house. Then you deposit materials stage by stage and pick Build (a 2 second hold per work unit) to raise the shell. Only the owner and invited key holders can build there. The four plots cost $1,400, $1,750, $2,000 and $2,250 at the alpha price.

Map

The label on the map is the home's code and its alpha price in thousands. Prices are the alpha price (50 percent of the list).

Paint bay (Saint-Philippe east districts, the mechanic's workshop yard)Drive your own car onto the pad beside the bench and walk up to the bench: one row per paint job for your car, with its price (a livery $250 to $400; a police livery shows only to police; a car with no paint job on offer shows only the hint row). Pick a row and the car comes back on the pad in the new paint, keeping its key, plate, lock and cargo. No window
GarageCar parts $200, repair kit $80. Buys scrap metal $4, copper wire $12, rubber scrap $5
Filling station pumps$2 per liter. Pick Fill the tank with your car at the pump
BarberA haircut
CafeDrinks and snacks; chess table beside it
Market stallBuys your apple juice, cabbage, honey and planks: look at the stall and scroll, one Sell row per good you carry with its price, plus Sell all goods. No inventory window
Dock wholesale yardBuys planks, boards, posts, firewood, cement, coal and metal bars in bulk; price falls as you sell and recovers hourly. Also buys every fish and smoked fish at a fixed price (a trout is $8, a smoked tuna $43; see Jobs)
Timber counterBuys planks $8 and hardwood boards $15 (a purse that refills through the hour)

What the clothing store and the gun store carry

  • Clothing store: 65 items, with a rack and a workwear counter. Shirts $25 to $30, trousers $35 to $170, jackets $30 to $250, three raincoat colors $60, 26 hats and caps $15 to $38 (flat caps, knitted hats, trucker caps, berets, ushanka, hard hats), work boots $40 and $48, gloves $15 to $20, watches $35 and $45, and rucksacks priced by size: canvas sack $28, Swiss M70 $30, Kolobok $60, ALICE $80, field pack $110. No military uniforms; the Rally gear belongs to a game DLC the shop cannot sell. The dressed mannequins sell what they wear: scroll on one for each piece and its price, or the whole outfit at the sum, and press F; if your pockets are full the piece is left at your feet.
  • Gun store: Pistol PM $350 and Rifle M21 $1,500 (a permit is needed); magazines $15 to $35; scopes $300 and $450; holsters $25 and $30; a magazine pouch $25; the gang radio $60. Scopes, holsters and pouches are sold to anyone. The vz. 58 and the M9 are not on the counter (the vz. 58 is a black market rifle at $1,800). The self-serve shelf sells a ushanka at $38, the same price as the clothing store.
  • Item names: every shop row has a plain name. The hardware store lists an Entrenching tool, the pharmacy Aspirin, Gauze roll, Sterile gauze pack, Buckle tourniquet and Rubber tourniquet, the farm supply a Reaper and the clothing rack names each color and variant (Cotton shirt, red plaid; Ushanka, flaps up and flaps down; Wristwatch, brown strap). A shop or car lot price list shows six to eight rows at a time, and each lot titles its own list, for example Truck yard - price list.

6. Police

Police are players. There is no roster to wait for in the alpha: anyone can sign up at the station and start the same minute.

Join and go on duty

  1. Go to the police station on the main street (east of the square; the gun store is next door). Press F at the duty desk (the punch clock).
  2. First time only: pick Apply. In the alpha the desk approves you on the spot.
  3. Pick Clock in. Your civilian clothes and pack are stored and you swap into the police kit: cap, dark turtleneck, trousers, officer harness, boots, an M9 pistol with two magazines, the station car key, a pager, handcuffs and a radio. Clock out at the same desk to swap back.
  4. If you die on duty your shift ends; you keep the police gear and your civilian things come back when you respawn.
  5. Your pager beeps with each dispatch call. When a car owner reports their car stolen, it also shows a line with the plate and the car. The line stays on the pager until an officer recovers the car or a chop shop scraps it.

Pay is handed over in cash when you clock out, by the second you were on duty, plus your bonus. One clock-in counts at most 3 hours of pay and rank time, and time away from the game or standing idle does not count. Clock out and in again for a fresh shift.

RankPay per hourBonus cap per hourFine limitOn duty to rise
Cadet$350$100$5001 hour
Patrol$375$100$1,0002 hours
Senior Patrol$400$100$2,5004 hours
Sergeant$425$95$4,0008 hours
Lieutenant$450$70$5,000top

Bonus: a call closed as resolved (fine the suspect at the scene, or radio it from the car) earns $15, a suspect booked at the desk $10, and a stolen car recovered to its owner $20 (not your own car). The bonus stops at your rank's cap each hour and is paid with your shift when you clock out. It survives a server restart. Fines go to the town, never to you.

A higher rank also promotes: at the armory, an officer above the new rank can promote you. Higher ranks draw bigger weapons (the M16A2, then the AKS-74U).

The car

Three police cars (covered UAZ469 with a blue light bar) stand beside the station. The station car key in your kit opens and starts every one of them. Press F6 to lock or unlock a car (gamepad: press the right stick). Cycle the siren modes with the right mouse button (gamepad: click the left stick). Station cars are not owned: they are back at the station after a restart.

Car pool board. On duty, press F at the car pool board and pick your rank's car ("Take the Cadet car": a white S105; "Take the Patrol car": the white UAZ469 with POLICE on the doors, Patrol and up). It stands in the bay in front of the board, unlocked for officers on duty. Taking another car sends your last one back, unless someone is sitting in it. A car above your rank is grayed out with the rank it needs.

Stop, cuff, search, arrest

An arrest is five steps: cuff, escort, put in vehicle, drive to the station, book into jail at the cell.

  • Search: face a player within 2 m, press F to open the player menu and pick Search. Every item they carry is checked. Anything illegal for them is seized and filed as an offense. A pistol with a firearm permit is left alone. You see "Seized from <name>: ..." when something is taken.
  • Search a car: stand by a stopped car and pick Search vehicle. Cartons, bottles and other contraband in the trunk show up by class: "Found in the trunk: 2 tobacco, 1 alcohol". Search again within 5 minutes to seize them; the people in the car are charged. Legal goods stay in the car.
  • Cuff: hold the handcuffs in your left hand and pick Cuff (a 2 second hold) on a player who is downed, stunned, held up, or has their hands up and no weapon. A cuffed player can walk but cannot hold anything. Uncuff frees them; you get the cuffs back. Cuffing a wanted player puts a "Jail booking" waypoint on your screen: that is where you book them.
  • Radar gun: hold the radar gun, aim at a car (up to 150 m) and pick Measure speed. A toast shows the speed and the limit, and the class: minor (1 to 15 km/h over), road (16 to 30 over) or serious (over 30). Each class is a law-book charge. The gun is not issued in the kit yet.
  • Escort: pick Escort on a cuffed suspect to walk them along. An uncuffed suspect cannot be escorted.
  • Put in vehicle: at a police car pick Put in vehicle to seat your suspect, then drive to the station. At the station pick Take out of vehicle; they step out beside the car, still yours.
  • Book into jail: walk the cuffed suspect to the cell door (the waypoint). Their action list then shows Book into jail: full sentence and Book into jail: reduced (cooperated) (half, at least 30 seconds). Pick one: they go into the cell, the cuffs come back to you. Booking is only offered at the jail.
  • Law book: a book lies open on a desk at the station. Anyone can scroll on it and pick Read: Criminal, Read: Traffic, Read: Narcotics or Read: Weapons. The page lists that section's codes with the fine and the time for each; a code marked jail only has no fine. These are the amounts the booking desk charges.
  • Booking desk: stand at the booking desk with the cuffed suspect beside you and pick Book suspect. The charge sheet opens on your screen: one row for each open crime report. Tick the charges (a charge that stacks under a higher one, or that would pass your rank limit, is grayed; a row over your limit shows its own fine and the word capped), check the Total fine and Time in the cell at the foot, and press Sign. The suspect then sees Pay $X now and Take the time (N min) on the desk and picks one. Paying takes the fine from the cash they carry first and their bank for the rest; the cuffs come off, the charges are cleared and they walk free. The money goes to the town, never to you. A suspect who can't cover the fine, or who takes the time, goes to the cell. A charge with only a fine still costs cell time when refused: a minute for every $60, at most 15 minutes. One booking at a time per suspect. Paid or jailed, the signed sheet takes the licenses its charges carry (reckless driving takes the driving license for 3 days, brandishing the firearm permit for 7; days are game days, 2 real hours each), and the suspect is told which and for how long. The license desk in the station porch turns a banned player away until the days run out.
  • Tickets: pick Write ticket to hand a paper fine. The pad lists the offenses your rank may fine, priced in minutes of a civilian's work: minor road $50 to $75 (speeding up to 15 over, parking, inspection), road $150 to $250 (speeding 16 to 30 over, reckless driving, an overloaded vehicle), serious road $300 to $400 (speeding more than 30 over, a crash, driving without a license), weapons $250 to $800. Robbery, murder and the other violent charges are jail only, 10 to 15 minutes. Up to three unpaid tickets per person.
  • Spike strips and roadblocks are in the kit.
  • Hands up: a suspect presses F7 (gamepad: right bumper + X). That counts as complying, so you can search and cuff them.

Jail, fines and the wanted board

  • The cell is inside the station; its gate reads "The cell is locked" to anyone who tries it. A sentence is 60 seconds per wanted level, at most 15 minutes. When it ends the wanted level drops by one. Time in jail counts online time: it pauses when you log out and survives a restart. A prisoner sees "Jail: m:ss left" at the top of their screen, and the cell door opens when it reaches zero.
  • A prisoner can work off time: the laundry tub, the kitchen sink and the yard broom each take 24 to 30 seconds off after a short job (scaled to the 15 minute cap), with a 30 second wait between repeats of the same chore.
  • Bail: a prisoner can use the bail phone in the cell to pay bail from their bank and walk out at once. Bail is $150 per minute left, at least $500. Not enough in the bank, no bail; cash does not count.
  • A ticket is paid at the punch clock of the station duty desk, in cash, oldest first. After 30 minutes unpaid it doubles. After another 30 minutes the person gets +1 wanted and a poster on the wanted board.
  • The wanted board and the case board inside the station list who is wanted and why. The dispatch board shows reports from payphones.

Calls, evidence and the armory

  • Players call you from a payphone: Report a crime, Report an emergency or Report someone suspicious. An on-duty officer hears it on the radio and sees it on the board. The call also waits at the dispatch board: Take a call hands it to you with a waypoint to the phone it came from.
  • Close a call from the car. After you take a call at the dispatch board, drive to the scene and use the radio rows at the driver door of your police car (the Cadet S105, the Patrol UAZ or the S1203 van): Radio: call resolved, Radio: no one found or Radio: call unfounded. You must be within 50 m of the scene. Only resolved earns the bonus, and never for a call you phoned in yourself. If you hold more than one call, the radio closes the one you are parked at.
  • A player whose phoned-in calls are closed as unfounded three times in one day is charged with emergency line abuse, and their calls show as low priority on the board until the next day.
  • On the radio, a dispatcher reads each call to you after a short squelch: what happened, then the place ("Robbery in progress. At the general store."). The written line follows on screen. A caller can ring once a minute; with nobody on duty nothing connects.
  • The armory hands out kit by rank. The evidence locker is in the station.
  • A fired alarm at the bank, a shop till or the cash van also goes to dispatch.

The station, the cars and the gun store are on the Saint-Philippe map and the crime map.

7. Crime

Crime pays more than a day job and costs more when it goes wrong. Everything here raises your wanted level (1 to 5), which the police see on the wanted board. A wanted player can be arrested; the cell time is 60 seconds per level, 15 minutes at most. New characters are refused for their first 5 minutes of play, so you cannot rush in before you have found your feet.

Wanted level

OffenseAdds
Robbing a till+1
Shoplifting+1
Breaking into a building+1
Stealing a car (not by force)+1
Cash van or armory or bank heist+1 each
Robbing a hospital+1
Stealing a weapon+2
Carrying an unlicensed item+1
Carrying a restricted item+2
Carrying an illegal item (a search finds it)+2
Carjacking (taking a car by force)+3
Murder+3
An unpaid fine that has run late+1
Chop shop, lockpick, moonshine0, but on your record

The level is capped at 5. An arrest sentence ends with one level removed.

Robbery

  • Fuel station till. Draw a weapon and talk to the attendant; a robbery reply appears only while a weapon is out. A hold timer with a bar starts and warns you if you leave its radius. If it pays you get $150 in cash. A downed attendant ends the hold unpaid.
  • Supermarket till. Pays $120 to $180, same rules. Both tills have a cooldown after a robbery and refuse if you have no room to carry the cash.
  • General store box safe. A small olive steel safe stands behind the counter of the general store in Saint-Philippe. It needs at least 1 police officer on duty. It opens after a short fuse, sounds the store alarm and pays a little cash ($120). After a haul it stays shut for 45 minutes; a second try in that time is refused.
  • Supermarket box safe. The Saint-Philippe supermarket has the same olive steel safe behind its till, with the same rules: at least 1 police officer on duty, a short fuse, the store alarm, $120, and a 45 minute wait after a haul.
  • Bakery, butcher and cafe tills. Each pays $120, same rules as the other tills.
  • Weapons and cars. Stealing a weapon adds +2; taking a car by force adds +3. Only civilians can do either; the police see it at once.
  • Crew tills. Where a till needs a crew, Start the job gathers every armed civilian within 15 m.
  • Hospital till. Robbing it adds +1 and rings the hospital alarm.

Everyone sees the alarm on the map. While a till, the bank vault, the clinic cabinet or the armory is being robbed, its badge on the map (M) has a pulsing red ring with a "!" for about three minutes after the alarm; then it turns gray for fifteen minutes ("Robbed recently"). Hover the badge to see when the alarm went off; the map key on the right lists it as Alarm. Police still get their own radio call.

Lockpicks, drills and the fence

The fence (map name Fence, off the public map, in a yard just east of the square) sells crime tools only to people with a record:

ToolPriceCrimes needed
Lockpick$2500
Police scanner$9002
Drill$2,5003
Keycard$1,5008
Breaching charge$4,0005

A lockpick opens a house or shop door (+1 break-in, and a witness can call it in). The fence also buys stolen car parts at half price.

License bans. A conviction can take a license for a number of game days (2 real hours each): stealing a car takes the driving license for 14 days, carjacking for 21, a speeding ticket for 2. Robbery takes the firearm permit for 14 days, stealing a weapon for 14, an armory heist for 30, and murder takes both licenses for 30.

The north outpost

A rebel outpost stands about 4 km from Saint-Philippe. Inside its fence is a safe zone: nobody fights there. It has gate guards, a quartermaster, a contraband buyer and a chalk board by the fire. On-duty police are turned away at the traders; off-duty police are served.

The quartermaster does not know you at first. What he sells grows with your standing in the underworld (Unknown, Known, Trusted, Respected; the game never shows a number): a gang radio ($60) for anyone, a pistol ($450) once you are Known, a rifle (AK-74, $2,000) once you are Trusted. A better piece is refused in words until then. Crime, gang work and trading at the outpost raise the same standing. Bar staff at the Chotain and Levie bars may pass on a tip once the town knows you; the place is marked on your map for that shift only.

Chop shop

No car on the island is free. Every car you do not own is locked: the cars parked around town, the display cars at the car lot, the cab at the taxi rank, the woodlot truck, the cash van and the depot tanker. Trying the door says "Vehicle is locked". Police cars open only for an officer on duty. A company truck or the depot tanker opens only for the player doing that job. A parked Skoda 105 takes a lockpick and then a hotwire, and that is a crime.

Steal a car, drive it to a chop bench, and take it apart: hold Work for 6 units. You get 30 percent of its value, up to $3,000, plus car parts (2). A chop bench has a 5 minute cooldown. A stolen UAZ469 is worth $750; the M923A1 truck $2,400; a T601 $210.

There are two benches: in the fence yard in town, and at the barn compound (see the map) on the country road south-east of town. The fence yard is closer to the police station.

#PlaceWhat
60Chop yardChop stolen cars (a back-country bench).
61Still barn: mash barrelsMash plums and cabbage.
62Still barn: the stillDistill the mash into moonshine.
63Still barn: packing benchPack bottles into crates.
64Still barn: launderingWash marked cash, keep 65 percent.

Moonshine

Everything is at the still barn in the barn compound. Three mash barrels, one still and one packing bench.

  1. Mash: load plums or cabbage into a barrel and hold Work (12 units; more hands finish sooner).
  2. Distill: put the mash in the still and hold Work (16 units). Collect a bottle of moonshine.
  3. Pack: at the bench hold Work (10 units) to make a contraband crate.
  4. Sell at a buyer spot (three in town, off the public map). A bottle is worth about $60.

The work can go wrong: a 6 percent chance on each work tick. Three strikes ruin the batch and the barrel explodes, hurting anyone close. The barn also gives off smoke and heat that police can follow. Some chains need a license or equipment; the refusal says which.

Laundering

Crime cash on this server is marked. Wash it at the laundry station in the still barn: you keep 65 percent (the washer takes a 35 percent cut), up to $1,500 a batch, a batch takes 90 seconds, and there is a daily cap of $6,000.

Pharmacy cabinet

The drug cabinet in the clinic is a big job, like the bank. It opens only when at least one medic or two police officers are on duty, and only when no other big job is underway on the island. Otherwise the cabinet tells you why when you look at it. Once your charge is armed on the cabinet, the job holds the island's big-job slot for about 15 minutes; after that the pharmacy stays shut to robbers for 2 hours (the cabinet says how many minutes are left). The clinic runs short of medicine for a while afterwards (see the medic chapter).

Bank heist

Needs at least 2 police on duty. You have 12 minutes.

The bank is a big job: only one big job (the bank or the hospital pharmacy) runs on the island at a time. The job starts the moment your charge is armed on the staff door, so a second crew cannot arm another big job while your fuse burns. While another one is underway, the staff door tells you so and cannot be armed. If the police defuse your charge before it goes off, the job still counts. After a bank job ends, paid out or not, the bank stays shut to robbers for 3 hours (the door says how many minutes are left).

  1. Staff door. Breach the bank's staff door (lockpick or charge). The alarm rings, dispatch hears, and the clerk may put their hands up.
  2. Vault. Open the vault with a drill or a breaching charge. Money bags spill on the floor. Carry them: dropping a bag leaves the cash in the world.
  3. Getaway. Every crew member must get more than 120 m from the bank before the clock runs out.

The cash van is easier and smaller. It parks at three stops in town for 5 minutes at a time (it moves if nobody is within 40 m). Open its cash box with a drill or a charge; money bags spill beside it. It counts as +1 wanted and sets off the van alarm.

Jailbreak

Breaking someone out takes two breaching charges.

  1. Outer door. Charge the jail's outer door. The fuse is 20 seconds. The alarm rings and dispatch hears where.
  2. Cells. With the outer door open, charge the cell door (15 seconds). The cells cannot be charged while the outer door is still shut.

When the cells blow, every prisoner in the cell is free: their sentence ends, and they are wanted for escaping custody. Whoever set the cell charge gets +4 wanted for the jailbreak. A prisoner cannot set a charge from inside. The doors seal themselves again after 10 minutes (police can repair them sooner), and the jail cannot be charged again for an hour after a break.

Hideouts

Two contested sites (a hideout on the hilltop mast and the farm compound) are fought over by organizations. Organizations are run from the registry cabin in town (map name Organization office, with the flag wall outside): the registrar founds a crew for $250, takes joins and files notices, and the war board there lists the fights. A war declaration costs $2,500 from the crew's fund; the other crew has 15 minutes to answer, a war lasts 2 hours, and the same two crews can fight once a day. Each site has a flag pole: it flies the flag of the gang that holds the site, with the gang's name on the board below, and a plain white cloth when nobody does. Pick a new flag at the flag wall and your poles change within a few seconds.

Recruit face to face. Look at a player with no organization and pick Invite to <name> from the action list. They look back at you and pick Join <name> or Decline <name>; an offer lapses after 2 minutes. A leader looking at a member picks Remove from <name>. Nobody can remove the founder.

A new recruit is a prospect for the first 48 hours (real time, restarts included): they ride with the crew and use the gang radio, but cannot take money from the fund or open the stash. A leader can promote them early.

A gang radio keeps the crew on its own channel. Carry one and pick Tune to gang channel from its action list: your crew hears you and nobody else does, even on the same frequency. When someone leaves or is removed, the channel changes and the radios of members who are online follow it; if you were away, or after a server restart, pick Tune to gang channel again.

Your map shows where every online member of your organization is, updated every few seconds, and nobody outside the crew sees these marks. A member who is downed, jailed or cuffed shows in gray. While you are jailed or cuffed yourself, the crew's marks disappear from your map and come back once you are free. A member who leaves or is removed drops off everyone's map at once.

3Bank (vault)Bank heist: staff door, vault, getaway.

8. Medic and clinic

When you are shot

A lethal hit knocks you down; it does not kill you. While you are down you cannot move or act and take no more damage. Other players can search you.

  • You have 3 minutes before you bleed out.
  • A bandage adds 30 seconds, a tourniquet 45 seconds and a saline bag 60 seconds. Anyone can use them on you. Morphine does not add time.
  • A medic on duty can Revive you if they reach you in time (within 2.5 m). A medic or an on-duty officer can load you into a car to get you to the clinic when a vehicle with a free seat is next to you.
  • After 30 seconds you can give up: hold X (gamepad Y). That counts as death. Logging out while down also counts.

After dying

You wake in a hospital bed in the clinic. A paper bill for $150 is put in your pack. Pay it at the hospital till: your money in the bank is never touched. What you carried stays with your body where you died. A revive by a medic costs $100 (half of it goes to the medic).

The clinic

The clinic (map name Clinic, sign Everon Village Hospital) is the converted town house next to the taxi rank, just north of the main street. It has a waiting room, a reception counter, two hospital beds, the medic duty desk and a medicine cabinet. The pharmacy north of the clinic sells aspirin ($10), gauze ($8) and tourniquets ($25) over the counter; saline bags ($60) and morphine ($80, medics only) come from the pharmacy counter.

Working as a medic

  1. Go to the medic duty desk in the clinic and press F to Clock in. Anyone may sign on; there is no roster. Your civilian things are stored and you take the medic kit.
  2. Wait at the clinic or patrol. The medic dispatch board lists calls. Revive downed players and bring patients in.
  3. Clock out at the same desk. You are paid in cash for the time you were on duty. One clock-in counts at most 3 hours of pay and rank time, and time away from the game or standing idle does not count; clock out and in again for a fresh shift.
RankPay per hourBonus cap per hourAdds to your kitOn duty to rise
Orderly$480$40Dressing, tourniquet1 hour
EMT$500$50Saline bag2 hours
Paramedic$530$50Morphine4 hours
Doctor$560$40Surgical gauzetop

Reviving and delivering patients earns medic job experience and a bonus: $10 a revive and $15 a patient put in a hospital bed (the bed's own revive is included, so a bed delivery is $15, not $25). Reviving yourself earns nothing. A hurt resident from a medic call also counts: hold Treat the patient beside them (about 8 s, one field dressing). They get up and walk off, the call closes and you earn the $10 revive bonus once per patient. The bonus stops at your rank's cap each hour and is paid with your shift when you clock out.

Casualty calls. Casualty calls come in on the board while you are on duty. About every 20 minutes a hurt resident goes down at a work site (a mine, the woodlot, the farm compound, the dock or the roadside fuel stop) and the call shows on the clinic's medic board and your pager with the place and what happened ("Miner down at the mine, crushed hand"). Drive there, revive them or carry them to the ambulance. One call per medic on duty, two at most; an untreated call leaves the board after a while and the resident is gone.

Ambulance pool board. On duty, press F at the ambulance pool board and pick your rank's ambulance ("Take the Orderly ambulance": the white UAZ452 with AMBULANCE on the sides, Orderly and EMT; "Take the Paramedic ambulance": the white S1203, Paramedic and Doctor). It stands in the bay in front of the board, unlocked for medics on duty only. Taking another one sends your last back, unless someone is sitting in it. The board lists only the ambulances your rank may take.

The clinic, the taxi rank, the pharmacy and the notice board are on the Saint-Philippe map.

When the clinic is short. Break into the clinic's drug cabinet and the pharmacy runs out of stock for a while. A paper notice appears beside the clinic's front door ("Pharmacy closed: Stock stolen. Medicine: Prices raised. Until: Further notice"), the counter charges more and a revive near the clinic takes longer. The notice comes down when the clinic is stocked again.

Police, medic and fishing

ActionHow
Cuff, uncuffhold the prompt in the player menu (about 2 seconds); handcuffs in your left hand
Search, arrest, write ticketthe player menu: press F on the player

The F10 key opens a developer menu that works only on a server that turns it on. You will not use it.

Admin commands (server staff only)

An administrator types these in the chat after #login <admin password>. Anyone else is refused.

CommandWhat it does
#lfmoney <player id or name> <amount>Give cash to a player who is online; a negative amount takes cash back. Up to $1,000,000 a call
#lfmoney <player id or name> <amount> bankThe same, on the bank balance

The amount is saved like any other change to a balance. #players shows the player ids.
